[MUQATIL:18:9-10/r4] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | The young men ask for mercy from God, which Muqatil glosses as provision from Him.
[MUQATIL:18:9-10/r5] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | They ask God to prepare right guidance in their affair; rushd here means facilitation, and the wording involves fronting.
[YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p173/r1] YAHYA-SALLAM, d. 200 · السدي | reports | Al-Suddī interprets the mercy the youths ask for as provision and 'from You' as from God's presence.
[YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p173/r2] YAHYA-SALLAM, d. 200 · author | holds | The youths were believers who fled their unbelieving people, fearing they would be killed for their faith.
[FARRA:v2p134/r5] FARRA, d. 207 · author | holds | The hamza in هيئ is written on an alif here; normally a hamza is seated according to the preceding vowel, though Arabs sometimes use alif in every position.
[FARRA:v2p134/r6] FARRA, d. 207 · author | reports | The ʿAbd Allāh codex reportedly wrote شيأ and يستهزأون with alif in positions where the more common orthography uses another seat.
[FARRA:v2p134/r7] FARRA, d. 207 · author | holds | The first spelling pattern is more common in books, although the alif spelling is analogical to the word’s origin.
[TUSTARI:18:10/r1] TUSTARI, d. 283 · author | holds | The youths’ request for mercy means asking God to preserve them in remembrance of Him.
[TAB-FULL:v15p161/r1] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | The youths took refuge in the mountain cave to flee their people while preserving their religion; they asked God for mercy from Him and guidance toward the right course. | mentions 18:9
[TAB-FULL:v15p161/r2] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | Their request for a rightly directed course means that God make easy what pleases Him and their escape from disbelief and idol worship, and guide them to sound action. | mentions 4:6
[TAB-FULL:v15p161/r3] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · عمرو | reports | The youths followed Jesus, while their idolatrous king pressed them to worship idols; they refused and withdrew to a cave to protect their faith. | mentions 18:14
[TAB-FULL:v15p161/r4] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · عمرو | reports | One youth proposed his father's cave as refuge; the people sealed them inside, then a later Christian king removed the barrier, whereupon they awoke and estimated they had slept a day or part of one. | mentions 18:14, 18:19
[TAB-FULL:v15p164/r1] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · ابن إسحاق | reports | Ibn Ishaq relates that Christian belief had weakened amid sin and idolatrous rulers; Deqianus persecuted those who retained Jesus' religion, forcing the faithful to flee or face death and mutilation.
[TAB-FULL:v15p164/r2] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · ابن إسحاق | reports | The young nobles sought God's help through prayer, fasting, charity, praise, and tears as persecution intensified; they were freeborn youths from prominent Roman families.
[TAB-FULL:v15p164/r3] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · مجاهد | reports | Mujahid reports that at least one youth still showed a downy beard because he was so young.
[TAB-FULL:v15p164/r4] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn Abbas says they were eight, naming Mكسلمينا as the eldest and the one who spoke to the king, followed by the other named youths.
[TAB-FULL:v15p166/r1] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | reports | As Deqianus prepared a citywide sacrifice to idols, the youths prayed for the believers' deliverance; informers found them prostrate and reported their disobedience to the king. | mentions 18:14
[TAB-FULL:v15p166/r2] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | reports | The king summoned the eight tearful, dust-covered youths and demanded that they sacrifice to his gods or be killed.
[TAB-FULL:v15p168/r1] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | reports | Deqianus strips the youths of their rank and jewelry but postpones punishment, giving the young men time to reconsider their refusal.
[TAB-FULL:v15p168/r2] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | reports | Fearing the king's return, each youth takes money from his father's house, gives some away, and sets out for a nearby mountain cave; their dog follows.
[TAB-FULL:v15p168/r3] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | reports | They devote themselves to worship in the cave and entrust their provisions to Yemliha, who secretly enters town disguised as a poor man to buy food and learn news.
[TAB-FULL:v15p168/r4] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | reports | When Deqianus returns to Ephesus and orders sacrifices, Yemliha reports that the youths have been found and are sought, alarming his companions.
[TAB-FULL:v15p170/r1] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | reports | The youths prostrate themselves, pray for protection from persecution, and eat the small meal Yemliha brought as evening falls.
[TAB-FULL:v15p170/r3] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | reports | Deqianus searches for the missing youths and tells the nobles he would have forgiven them if they repented, but the nobles urge him to question their parents and punish them.
[TAB-FULL:v15p173/r1] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | reports | The two secret believers, Bedros and Ronas, record the youths' names, lineages, and story on lead tablets in a sealed copper chest by the cave, hoping future believers will find them.
[TAB-FULL:v15p174/r1] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · عبد الله بن عبيد بن عمير | reports | They were richly dressed young princes who encountered one another while leaving a festival where their people carried idols; each had independently received faith from God and feared persecution.
[TAB-FULL:v15p174/r2] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · عبد الله بن عبيد بن عمير | reports | The youths cautiously paired off to test one another's beliefs, discovered that all shared faith, and entered a nearby cave with their hunting dog, where God made them sleep for 309 years. | mentions 18:11, 18:16
[TAB-FULL:v15p174/r3] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · عبد الله بن عبيد بن عمير | reports | Their people searched for them but could not find the cave; they later recorded the youths' names and lineage, and a Muslim king succeeded the earlier ruler after generations passed. | mentions 18:11
[TAB-FULL:v15p174/r4] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | reports | Another reported explanation says they fled a ruler's pursuit after one of them was accused of committing a crime.
[TAB-FULL:v15p175/r1] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · وهب بن منبه | reports | Wahb relates that a disciple of Jesus converted young nobles while working at a bath; after the king's son and a woman died there, the blamed disciple and youths fled with a farmer and dog, slept in a cave, and were sealed inside by the king. | mentions 18:11
[ZAJJAJ:v3p270/r3] ZAJJAJ, d. 311 · author | holds | Awaw means they went to the cave and made it their refuge; fitya is a collective plural like ghilma and sabiyaa, but the pattern is not productive.
[ZAJJAJ:v3p270/r4] ZAJJAJ, d. 311 · author | holds | They ask for mercy meaning forgiveness and provision, and for guidance toward what draws them near God.
[ZAJJAJ:v3p270/r5] ZAJJAJ, d. 311 · author | prefers | Another vocalization of رشدا is possible, but رشدا suits the verse-ending pattern and means guidance toward what brings them near God.
[NAHHAS:v2p448/r4] NAHHAS, d. 338 · author | holds | The youths took refuge in the cave while fleeing for their faith and asked for mercy to save them from the unbelievers.
[NAHHAS:v2p448/r5] NAHHAS, d. 338 · author | prefers | Rushd means guidance by which they could be saved; rushd is preferred over rashad here to match the verse endings.
[SULAMI:v1p406#2/r1] SULAMI, d. 412 · سهل | reports | The youths' request for mercy asks for remembrance and gratitude in every state, while asking for the easiest path of divine enabling.
[SULAMI:v1p406#2/r2] SULAMI, d. 412 · جعفر | reports | Seeing the youths from one's own perspective brings flight, but seeing them from the Real's perspective reveals unity and lordship within them.
[SULAMI:v1p406#2/r3] SULAMI, d. 412 · ابن عطاء | reports | A view of all created things from one's own position would turn one's sight away from the youths; the Prophet is both a beholder of God and beheld from Him.
[SULAMI:v1p406#2/r4] SULAMI, d. 412 · ابن عطاء | reports | The youths were surrounded by lights of the Real, exaltation, and awe, explaining why the Prophet would flee if he saw them.
[SULAMI:v1p406#2/r5] SULAMI, d. 412 · الحسين | reports | The Prophet would recoil from the overpowering spiritual states displayed in them, despite recognizing their lofty station of nearness and witnessing.
[SULAMI:v1p406#2/r6] SULAMI, d. 412 · جعفر | reports | The awe of God's power, care, and guardianship over them would be unbearable; the flight would truly be from God, since what appears in them comes from Him.
[SULAMI:v1p406#2/r7] SULAMI, d. 412 · جعفر | reports | One flees when looking from the human self but stands firm when looking from God; the Prophet's flight from unbelievers reflects the former human perspective.
[SULAMI:v1p406#2/r8] SULAMI, d. 412 · بعضهم | reports | Angelic lights are honors, while human lights are guidance, outward and inward; their greater awe explains the report that Satan fled from ʿUmar.
[THALABI:v6p147/r1] THALABI, d. 427 · ابن إسحاق | reports | Ibn Ishaq narrates that pagan Roman ruler Decius persecuted Christians in Ephesus; eight noble youths kept monotheism, prayed and fasted, then fled the forced choice between idol worship and death after believers were tortured and displayed on the city walls.
[THALABI:v6p147/r2] THALABI, d. 427 · author | holds | The youths' prayer declares God alone as Lord of heaven and earth and says invoking another deity would be an outrageous falsehood; they ask for the persecution to be lifted.
[THALABI:v6p157/r2] THALABI, d. 427 · author | holds | The youths' taking refuge means going and joining the cave, a cavern in Mount Yanjalus called Khayram.
[THALABI:v6p157/r3] THALABI, d. 427 · author | holds | Their prayer asks God to ease for them what they seek of His good pleasure.
[THALABI:v6p157/r4] THALABI, d. 427 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn Abbas interprets right guidance as a safe way out of the cave.
[THALABI:v6p157/r5] THALABI, d. 427 · author | reports |

 Another interpretation takes rushd to mean correctness.
[THALABI:v6p204/r1] THALABI, d. 427 · معاذ | reports | The Prophet says reciting the beginning and end of Surat al-Kahf gives light from head to foot, while reciting all of it gives light from earth to heaven.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v3p286#2/r11] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · الحسن | reports | One account says the youths fled to the cave to preserve their religion.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v3p286#2/r12] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · مجاهد | reports | Another account says they were noble young men who met outside the city by chance; their eldest professed the Lord of heaven and earth, they agreed, then entered the cave and remained for three hundred years plus nine.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v3p286#2/r13] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · ابن قتيبة | reports | Ibn Qutaybah says they were Roman youths who entered the cave before Jesus; God put them to sleep, Jesus disclosed their story, and they were raised in the interval between Jesus and Muhammad.
[QUSHAYRI:v2p209/r1] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | holds | The youths were sheltered outwardly in a cave and inwardly under divine care; God took charge of them and brought spiritual states upon them while they were absent from themselves.
[QUSHAYRI:v2p209/r2] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | holds | Their prayer disavows their own power and sincerely turns to God; He answers, relieves their need, and gives them a good refuge.
[QUSHAYRI:v2p209/r3] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | holds | God effaced their self-awareness in the witnessing of unity and divine self-sufficiency, then returned them to sober discrimination after the state of union.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p537/r1] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · author | holds | The opening idh cannot attach to the preceding question because the youths' flight was long before the Prophet; it attaches to an omitted command, remember when they fled.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p537/r2] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · author | holds | The youths went to the cave and made it their shelter; Ibn Abbas says they fled there.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p537/r3] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · ابن عباس | reports | He glosses their going to the cave as fleeing to it.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p537/r4] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · author | holds | After fleeing those pursuing them, the youths prayed for mercy, understood here as forgiveness and provision.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p537/r5] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · ابن عباس | reports | They ask for mercy from God alone so that it will make them independent of everyone else.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p538/r1] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · author | holds | Hayyiʾ means set right or prepare; rushd and its related forms are the opposite of error.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p538/r2] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · أبو إسحاق | reports | He explains the prayer as asking for guidance to what brings one near to God and pleases Him; Ibn Abbas says to direct their deeds toward God's love.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p538/r3] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · أهل المعاني | reports | They parse the request as having an omitted noun, a thing of right guidance; further omission yields the sense, prepare what will enable us to attain guidance.
[WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:10-12/r1] WAHIDI-WAJIZ, d. 468 · author | holds | The youths fled to the cave from their pursuers, devoted themselves to supplication, and asked for forgiveness, provision, and guidance toward what brings them near God.
[JISHUMI:v6p4347/r2] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | Awā means to return, and maʾwā is a place of return or refuge.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p145/r1] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · محمد بن إسحاق بن يسار | reports | Ibn Isḥāq recounts that Christian society fell into grave error and idolatry under King Daqyānūs, who persecuted believers; eight elite youths fled, prayed for rescue, were captured, and refused the king's demand to worship idols, with Miksalmina speaking for them.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p155/r1] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · author | holds | Awā means they went to the cave and made it their dwelling; the cave was in Mount Banjulus and was called Khayram.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p155/r2] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · author | holds | The requested mercy means guidance in religion, or, by another view, provision.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p155/r3] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · author | holds | Hayyiʾ means make easy; rushd is what seeks God's approval and what brings right guidance.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p155/r4] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · ابن عباس | reports | He interprets rushd as a safe way out of the cave.
[KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p659/r7] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · author | holds | The requested mercy is from God's stores: forgiveness, provision, and safety from enemies; preparing their affair means guiding them as they leave unbelievers or setting their whole affair right.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p498#2/r1] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | reports | Reports describe the youths as sons of nobles in the city of the unbelieving king Daqiyus, also called Daqliyus or Daqinus; they were Romans and followers of Jesus, though another view places them before Jesus.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p498#2/r2] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | The youths' foreign names have weak transmission; al-Tabari's list gives Makselminya, Majseliniya, Tamlikha, Martus, Kashutunus, Birunus, Dinamus, and Yatūnus.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p498#2/r5] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | reports | One account says they hid their escape by playing with a polo mallet and ball as they moved toward the cave; another says they escaped while being taken to a festival.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p499#2/r1] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | reports | People recorded the youths' names, fathers, rank, and disappearance on lead or copper tablets; some say two secretly believing judges hid them, either at their homes or in the king's construction over the cave.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p499#2/r3] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | reports | The persecuting king is also said to have been a Roman ruler who sought to abolish the religion of Jesus and killed believers publicly.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p499#2/r4] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | The youths sought God's mercy, interpreted by commentators as provision, and a good way out of their situation; the author says this was a worldly prayer, while they trusted their afterlife outcome.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p499#2/r5] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | The majority read rashadan with both vowels open; Abu Raja reads rushdan with a rounded first vowel and silent second, while the majority reading better matches surrounding verse endings.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p499#2/r6] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | The words may also include mercy in the afterlife, and the author recommends this verse as a sufficient prayer for a believer's worldly needs.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p499/r1] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | reports | A separate account says the youths saw their city's festival idolatry, believed, and left the people to avoid sharing their punishment.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p499/r2] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · وهب بن منبه | reports | Wahb's account has a disciple of Jesus work in a bathhouse, convert the city's noble youths, then flee with them after the prince and a prostitute died there and the disciple was blamed.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p499/r3] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · عبيد بن عمير | reports | Ubayd ibn Umayr says the noble youths became believers one by one, met by chance beneath a tree, learned that their aims matched, and then fled together after confiding in pairs.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p499/r4] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | reports | Accounts say the dog belonged to a youth who hunted, or that a shepherd and his dog joined the group; its name is given as Himran or Qitmir.
[TABRISI:18:10-12/r1] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | The youths took refuge in the cave to escape their people and protect their religion, asking God for mercy, rescue, and a way to right guidance.
[TABRISI:18:10-12/r2] TABRISI, d. 548 · ابن عباس | reports | The prayer may ask God to provide a safe way out of the cave.
[TABRISI:18:10-12/r3] TABRISI, d. 548 · قيل | reports | Alternatively, they ask to be guided to a course that will save them, or for an arrangement that earns God’s approval.
[TABRISI:18:10-12/r4] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | The youths were believers who concealed Islam from a ruler named Daqiyānūs in Ephesus; he worshiped idols and killed opponents, though another account calls him a Magian who promoted that religion.
[TABRISI:18:10-12/r5] TABRISI, d. 548 · عبيد بن عمير | reports | ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr says the youths were close associates of the king who hid their faith from one another until they met, disclosed it, and fled to the cave.
[TABRISI:18:10-12/r6] TABRISI, d. 548 · قيل | reports | One account says they followed the religion of Jesus after the people of the Gospel had passed away; another places them before Jesus’s mission.
[TABRISI:18:9-12/r3] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | Awā means to return or take refuge; futiya is a collective plural for young men, like ṣabī/ṣibya and ghulām/ghilma, though such formations are not fully productive.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p108/r1] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · الزجاج | reports | Al-Zajjaj says āwaw ilayhi means they went to the cave and made it their refuge.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p108/r2] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | holds | Fitya is a plural of fatā, like ghulām/ghilma and ṣabī/ṣabiya; it is a collective form that does not generate parallel forms such as “ravens” or “wealthy men.”
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p108/r3] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | reports | Some commentators understand fitya to mean young men; Ibn Qutayba says fatā can mean a fully grown man, as in the verse about believing women.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p108/r4] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | holds | “From Your presence” means from You; raḥma means provision, and prepare our affair means set it right.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p108/r5] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | holds | Rushd means guidance toward what brings one near to God and is the opposite of error.

[RAZI-FULL:v21p70/r11] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Their prayer asks for mercy from God’s stores of grace, including guidance, knowledge, patience, provision, and safety from enemies.
[RAZI-FULL:v21p70/r12] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | “From Your presence” signals the greatness of the requested mercy, fitting God’s generosity and ample bounty.

[QURTUBI-FULL:18:10#2/r1] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · ابن عباس | reports | The dog was either their hunting dog or a shepherd's dog that followed the shepherd and youths; it was called Himran or Qitmir.
[QURTUBI-FULL:18:10#2/r2] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | reports | The youths' foreign names have weak transmission; al-Tabari lists Maksalmina as eldest spokesman and Yemlikha as the one sent with money, among six others.
[QURTUBI-FULL:18:10#2/r3] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · مقاتل | reports | The dog belonged to Maksalmina, the eldest youth and owner of sheep.
[QURTUBI-FULL:18:10#2/r4] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | The story establishes fleeing with one's religion and leaving family, homeland, wealth, and friends to escape persecution; the Prophet and Companions did likewise. | mentions 16:41, 9:20
[QURTUBI-FULL:18:10#2/r5] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | Retreat to mountains, caves, or solitude is a prophetic and saintly practice and is especially favored by many scholars amid fitna and corruption.
[QURTUBI-FULL:18:10#2/r6] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · العلماء | reports | Seclusion can be practiced in mountains, at coasts and frontier posts, or at home; a report advises hiding and guarding one's tongue during fitna.

[QURTUBI-FULL:18:10#2/r8] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · ابن المبارك | reports | Ibn al-Mubarak defines seclusion as joining people when they remember God and remaining silent when they discuss other matters.
[QURTUBI-FULL:18:10#3/r1] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · النبي ﷺ | reports | A report says the believer who mixes with people and patiently bears harm is better than one who avoids people and does not bear their harm.
[QURTUBI-FULL:18:10#3/r10] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | Any place away from people, including mosque retreat, coastal service, or home, fits the meaning of mountain solitude; mountains are named because they are common retreats.
[QURTUBI-FULL:18:10#3/r2] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · الحسن | reports | A saying that al-Baghawi transmits as a mursal report from al-Hasan and others calls believers' homes their cloisters.
[QURTUBI-FULL:18:10#3/r3] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · النبي ﷺ | reports | In response to Uqba ibn Amir asking about salvation, the Prophet advises holding the tongue, staying home, and weeping over one's sin.
[QURTUBI-FULL:18:10#3/r4] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · النبي ﷺ | reports | A Bukhari report describes a time when a Muslim's best property will be sheep taken to mountain heights and rain-fed places to flee fitna for faith.
[QURTUBI-FULL:18:10#3/r5] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · الحسن بن واقد | reports | A report attributed to the Prophet says that in year 180 AH celibacy, seclusion, and retreat to mountain tops become permitted for the community.
[QURTUBI-FULL:18:10#3/r6] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · الحسن | reports | A long report says that in a corrupt age only flight from peak to peak or stone to stone preserves religion; family may ruin a person by demanding unaffordable provision.
[QURTUBI-FULL:18:10#3/r7] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | prefers | People differ in capacity: mountain-cave retreat is the highest state, home seclusion suits others, and some can mix outwardly while remaining inwardly distinct.

[QURTUBI-FULL:18:10#3/r9] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · وهب بن منبه | reports | Wahb counsels a would-be recluse that people need one another, advising him to hear without listening, see without looking, and speak little.
[QURTUBI-FULL:18:10#4/r1] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · النبي ﷺ | reports | Uqba ibn Amir reports that God admires a shepherd on a mountain crag who calls and performs prayer from fear of Him, forgives him, and admits him to Paradise.
